spec_match.rationale: Exercises the exact new surface — the onanimationcancel IDL property vs addEventListener('animationcancel') on the same element — and feature-detects with `'onanimationcancel' in el`, the precise contract chromestatus/CSS Animations Level 1 describe.

interactive.rationale: Real controls (display:none, animation:none, restore, clear-log) drive a live pulse animation, per-method fired-status readouts, and a timestamped event log.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index blurb promises registering both methods and comparing which fires on cancellation; the page delivers exactly that.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers both major cancel triggers plus restore/re-trigger, and degrades honestly on pre-145 browsers with a clear NOT-supported banner (verified showing in Chromium 141).

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5160464445210624, MDN animationcancel, and the sibling cancel-triggers concept.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite asserts the new IDL attribute on Window and HTMLElement plus non-regression of the three pre-existing handlers; in Chromium 141 it honestly reports 4 pass / 2 fail (the two new-IDL assertions, a version gap, not a demo bug).

runtime_evidence.rationale: Load, honest fallback banner, animationstart logging, and clean console verified in headless Chromium 141; the property-handler firing path itself needs Chrome 145+ so the success path could not be observed here.

telemetry_health.rationale: The server injects /public/demo-telemetry.js (errors, unhandled rejections, clicks, LCP/CLS/INP) — verified present in the served DOM.

design_system.rationale: All colours come from the design-system variables; method-status fired state uses a color-mix of --accent-emerald over paper with black text.

accessibility.rationale: Controls are native buttons with visible text, but the event log and the two method-status readouts update without aria-live/role=log, so firings are invisible to screen readers.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: At a true 360px viewport the page is usable but content extends to 376px (an inline code fragment), clipped by the body overflow-x:hidden — a ~16px cut, no layout collapse (CDP-measured).

openQuestions.title: Announce cancel events to assistive tech
openQuestions.detail: The event log and the per-method status boxes change textContent only. Add role="log"/aria-live="polite" to #event-log and aria-live to the two .method-status readouts so the property-vs-listener comparison is perceivable without vision.

openQuestions.title: Fix ~16px mobile overflow from long inline code
openQuestions.detail: At 360px the documentElement scrollWidth is 376px (offending CODE right=375, clipped by body overflow-x:hidden). Allow the heading/inline code to wrap (overflow-wrap:anywhere on .method-col code) so nothing is cut on narrow phones.

summary: Strong, honest concept page: the exact new IDL surface is probed, both registration paths are compared with real controls, and the pre-145 fallback banner renders correctly (verified in this pre-145 browser). Feature conformance route reports 4 pass / 2 fail here, the 2 fails being the new-IDL assertions this browser genuinely lacks. Browser-verified with headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI (screenshot + DOM dump) and raw CDP (real click dispatch, console/network capture, 360x740 DPR3 mobile emulation) — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session. Chromium 141 predates Chrome 145, so v145-only API paths were validated on their fallback branches, not the new-API success path. The single failed fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet request is environmental (blocked host) and was not counted against any page.
